title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-16
content:
Context:
- Intermittent regressions on long-prefixed requests (seqlen > 4096) where attention kernel selection sometimes picks FlashAttention/optimized kernel and that path crashes or produces corrupted outputs when combined with KV cache reuse.
- Repro on staging: model=redwood-alpha-7b-v2 (quantized int8), deployment=dedicated-gpu-1 (A100), batcher=continuous-batching ON.

Symptoms observed:
- Worker logs show:
  - "AssertionError: KV cache shape mismatch: expected (layers, heads, seq, head_dim) but got (layers, heads, seq+1, head_dim)"
  - "cudaError: device-side assert triggered" (stack trace into flash_attention.cu)
  - Occasional segfault in worker -> restart and truncated streamed response.
- Correlates with reused KV cache sessions where appended completion > 512 tokens. Fresh sessions rarely fail.
- Corrupted tokens appear near the boundary where cached_seq + new_tokens crosses multiples of 128/256 (suspect tiling/alignment).

Commands / runs tried (chronological):
1) Baseline repro via staging API (curl) -> ~60% repro when reuse_kv_cache=true and long prefix.
   curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-7b-v2","input":"<VERY_LONG_PREFIX>","max_tokens":1024,"stream":true,"reuse_kv_cache":true}'

2) FORCED_ATTENTION_KERNEL=scaled_dot (force non-flash) -> no crash, slower but correct. Points to FlashAttention path.

3) Local microbench with same weights/quantization -> no crash on my devbox (CUDA driver 530.x). Staging uses 535.x. Driver/version difference notable.

4) Instrumented select_attention_kernel() to log choices and shapes -> observed selection of flash_attention_fast_path when seq_total>4096 and kv_reused==true with tile_size=128.

5) Added asserts before kernel launch -> failing runs show kv_append produced seq dimension off-by-1 (seq+1). Traced to kv_append() copy/range logic.

6) Stress tests with prefix lengths: 2048, 3072, 4096, 4097, 4608 -> failures cluster at 4097 and 4608 (crossing 4096 or non-multiple of 128).

7) Driver matrix: older driver 531.x passes; 535.x shows more failures. Suggests driver exposes UB or boundary check stricter.

8) cuda-memcheck on failing run -> device-side assert in flash_attention.cu boundary check (see JIRA INFR-2345 attached).

Quick hypotheses:
- A: Off-by-one in kv_append when handling vectorized copies crossing chunk boundary, leaving one extra token written -> flash kernel asserts.
- B: Kernel selection sometimes picks flash path for slightly misaligned buffers (race between selection and buffer resize).
- C: CUDA driver/kernel combo exposes UB that older drivers tolerated.
- D: Quantization/packing (int8) uses different stride/layout, bug in packing causes head_dim/stride mismatch.

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Force fallback to safe attention kernel for reused-KV + seq_total>4096 (staging only) -> incidents ~0%, latency +20%.
- Defensive check after kv_append: if shapes mismatch, reject request and clear KV -> prevents crash but degrades UX.

Investigation breadcrumbs (code areas):
- serving-runtime/src/attention/kernel_selector.cpp
- serving-runtime/src/attention/flash_attention.cu (stack ~line 842)
- serving-runtime/src/kv_cache/kv_cache.cpp (append/resize)
- quantization/pack_int8.cpp (packing into cache layout)
- CI repro job: infra/jobs/kv-seqlen-repro.yml
- Related PR: PR #812 (enable flash path for large seqlen)

Next actions / TODOs:
Short term (today/this week):
- Keep forced-fallback in staging for reused-KV + seq_total>4096. (Owner: infra/ops)
- Add unit tests for kv_append covering chunk boundary writes and a small repro harness that repeatedly appends across boundary. (Owner: Avery)
- Add debug hex dumps of last 3 KV rows pre/post-append for failing requests (redact PII). (Owner: Priya)

Medium term (1-2 weeks):
- Reproduce locally with identical CUDA driver 535.x and run under cuda-gdb to catch exact instruction. (Owner: Diego)
- Audit quantization packing for stride assumptions. (Owner: Avery + Diego)
- Add selection-logic guard: require buffer_stride % tile_size == 0 for flash path.

Long term:
- CI fuzz job that exercises kv append sizes + attention kernel combos across driver versions.
- Consider safe-mode for dedicated nodes disallowing aggressive flash kernels for reused-KV until validated.

Other observations:
- More likely when worker multiplexes clients and session pooling reuses KV (possible race on session.kv_lock).
- Introducing a 10ms sleep between kv_append and kernel launch in dev harness reduced failures -> suggests possible stream/sync issue; check streams and cudaMemcpy usage (async vs sync).

Immediate repro plan:
1) Collect 10 failure dumps with kernel debug logging + hex KV dumps on staging.
2) Run same workload on nodes with driver 531.x and 535.x to confirm driver dependency.
3) Instrument kv_append to write sentinel pattern at chunk boundary and verify after append; if sentinel corrupted -> copy/stride bug.

If you pick this up: start with kv_cache/kv_cache.cpp append() and kernel_selector heuristics. Ping Diego/Priya for staging creds or to flip forced-fallback.

Notes-to-self: keep this as scratchpad; once root cause fixed, write formal postmortem on Confluence and link from JIRA.
